title: Staged sweep config undo with telemetry hysteresis
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build an automated 'staged sweep' undo system for config changes that combines cost-aware batching/caching recommendations with robust automatic rollback triggers and state reconciliation. The system must reduce manual intervention for bad config deploys while avoiding flapping or unnecessary rollbacks that increase customer-visible churn.

Scope and motivations:
- Many recent regressions were caused by config tweaks (batching window, KV cache policy, kernel selection thresholds) that produced slow cost spikes or P99 regressions. We need a controller that can safely unwind such changes when telemetry indicates sustained negative impact.
- This ticket covers design and implementation of the controller, safe-apply flow (shadow/simulate + transactional snapshot), rollback triggers (multi-signal quorum + hysteresis), and reconciliation for runtime state (KV cache quarantines, batch in-flight drain, prefix replay). It also covers integration with the recommendations engine (suggested batching/cache profiles) so the controller can optionally apply suggested mitigations before full rollback.

Design summary (decisions made so far):
1) Staged sweep model: when a config change is applied, the controller performs an incremental sweep that escalates remediation steps: 1) apply non-disruptive mitigations (reduce batching window, increase cache TTL), 2) switch to fallback model variant or quantized kernel, 3) throttle new traffic to changed shard, 4) full rollback. Each step must be idempotent and reversible.
2) Triggering: triggers require a quorum of signals across three categories: latency (P95/P99 increase >= 15% sustained for 5m), correctness (increased error rate or functional test failures on canary), and cost (tokens/min or GPU-util cost jump >= 20% versus baseline). A single metric breach starts a hysteresis timer; only when the breach persists and at least two categories show anomalies do we start automated mitigation.
3) Hysteresis and anti-flapping: implement a time-weighted hysteresis window plus exponential backoff between automatic escalations. If a metric recovers, we abort escalation and record the incident for post-mortem.
4) Safe apply and snapshotting: every config apply creates an immutable snapshot (config diffs + routing table + KV-cache-epoch marker). The runtime supports 'prefix quarantine' that isolates affected KV keys until their consistency can be validated. Snapshots allow a deterministic rollback path and are stored with build metadata.
5) Reconciliation and state repair: after rollback, reconciliation tasks must repair KV cache mismatches and drain inflight batches. We'll implement a reconciliation queue that replays a bounded set of recent requests against the pre-change config in a shadow environment, validating outputs probabilistically before releasing quarantined prefixes.
6) Cost-aware prechecks: before an automated rollback we attempt a light mitigation pass using the Optimize engine's suggested batching/caching profile. If the suggested change resolves cost signal without impacting latency/correctness, we avoid a full rollback.

Trade-offs considered:
- Conservative thresholds reduce false positives but increase detection latency; we selected multi-signal quorum to balance sensitivity and false positives.
- Shadow replay increases fidelity but costs GPU cycles; we keep replay bounded to a sample size configurable by each customer tier.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for snapshot/rollback logic and idempotency.
- Integration test with local runtime harness: simulate config change that toggles batching/window and assert state snapshots and rollback restore KV checksum.
- Staging rollout: first enable controller as 'suggest' mode (logs decisions, no actions) for 2 weeks, then 'autopilot' in low-risk clusters (non-production partitions), then expand.

Metrics and dashboards:
- New dashboard: config-safety-overview (P95/P99, token-cost-per-minute, KV-cache-hit-rate, rollback-rate, time-to-rollback).
- Alerting rules: auto-rollback-notice (send PagerDuty for P0 autopilot rollbacks), suggested-mitigation (Slack to #runtime-safety for suggestions applied).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CFG/staged-sweep-undo-design
- Runtime PR for snapshot API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5482
- Dashboard prototype: https://dashboard.redwood.ai/d/CFG/config-safety-overview

Open questions / next actions:
- Threshold tuning per-customer: default vs enterprise-sla profiles. Plan: start conservative defaults and provide per-tenant knobs.
- How to surface mitigation decisions to customers (console experience): a later phase UI task tracked under console-2026.04.
- Locking semantics for snapshot/rollback when multiple config changes overlap; proposed approach: sequence numbers + optimistic compare-and-swap with conflict resolution policy.

Risks:
- Overaggressive autopilot could cause repeated rollbacks and customer confusion. Mitigation: staged rollout with manual review gates and clear console explanations.
- Shadow replay resource cost — will cap sample size and use low-priority GPU pools for replay.

acceptance_criteria: Controller can progress through mitigation steps automatically and log each action (suggest -> mitigation -> throttle -> rollback)
Snapshots are created for every config apply and can be used to fully restore system state within 3 minutes for affected partitions
Quorum-based triggers fire only when at least two signal categories exceed thresholds and anomalies persist past hysteresis window
KV prefix quarantine prevents serving inconsistent keys until reconciliation completes and reconciliation queue validates sample outputs
Integration tests cover rollback idempotency and no data corruption across shard boundaries
notes: Prefer conservative defaults for initial rollout. Coordinate with SRE for PagerDuty routing and with Customer Success for messaging to impacted customers when autopilot triggers.
